relevance_note: Case report of one girl with a de novo TNFAIP3 frameshift variant plus a literature table of previously reported patients: "We found that there was a heterozygous mutation (c.436_437deTC) in the TNFAIP3 gene".
method_note: Case report of one girl plus a literature summary (Table 1). Table 1 has 30 data rows; row 30 ("This case") is the case-report patient, recorded once under the label "patient" (Table 1 has no per-person label column, so the 29 earlier-reported people are "Table 1 row 1" to "Table 1 row 29"). A Python script transcribed Table 1 cells into the rows; the feature lists per row were written by hand and the transcription checked against the table. Table 1 fills the Pedigree, Mutation location and References columns only in the first row of each group, and the converted cells are empty in the following rows (not repeated). Following the rule that empty cells are not reported, the continuation rows have family_label, variant and source_reference_in_review = not reported; their variant rows are kept with variant_original_string 'not reported' because the table title ties every row to TNFAIP3 ("Clinical features of patients with TNFAIP3."). Many Family rows (3-11, 13) also have an empty References cell, so source is not reported for them. Possible misalignment in the paper: Family 1 is attributed to Shigemura et al [14], whose reference title names a C243Y mutation, while the c.728G > A p.Cys243Tyr variant is printed for Family 3; not resolved. Contradictions: (1) the text says Table 1 summarises "a total of 30 cases, including this case" but also "this case and the 48 cases reported so far"; n_patients_reported = 30 follows the table and the first statement. (2) For the patient, Table 1 lists genital ulcers and nonspecific rash, while the text says the parents denied vulvar ulcer, "No abnormalities were noted in the vulva and perianal areas" and "no skin rash": both rows emitted, checklist genital ulcers and skin lesions set to not reported. (3) Joint pain history was denied at admission, but knee pain, effusion and synovitis are reported at admission ultrasound and in May 2020; both rows emitted; arthritis checklist observed from synovitis/effusion. (4) Variant spelled c.436-437deTC (abstract), c.436_437deTC (case text, Table 1) and c.436_437delTC (Figure 4 legend); the Figure 4 form is recorded. Checklist choices: Table 1 'Fever' alone was not mapped to 'recurrent fever' (not stated as recurrent); 'intermittent fever' (row 13) was. 'Pericardial effusion', 'Recurrent pharyngitis', 'thrombophlebitis', 'stomatitis' and acne were not mapped to checklist items; 'cerebral palsy' and 'encephalopathy' were mapped to CNS involvement. 'Oral mucosa' in Table 1 (followed by 'genital ulcer') is read as oral mucosa ulcer. Patient: ANA 1:100 and anticardiolipin 18 RU/mL are printed without interpretation, so autoantibodies is not reported; ESR 58 mm/h at admission not called elevated in the text (CRP/PCT/WBC were stated as increased). The negative neurological examination and normal heart/lung examination are recorded as written and exclude no specific checklist item. Iron deficiency anaemia is not counted as autoimmune cytopenia. Age 2 years 3 months is the age at admission; follow-up continued to January 2021 without a stated age, so age at last evaluation and at diagnosis are not reported. Parents (father, mother) are in scope as relatives tested negative; no phenotypes reported for them (the mother's normal pregnancy and delivery is not a phenotype of hers). Country of the patient not stated (only the approving hospital).
